subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which minerals form the typical mafic composition of basalt?
options: Plagioclase + pyroxene + olivine (mafic)
Calcite and dolomite with minor quartz characteristic of carbonate rocks
Muscovite, biotite and quartz typical of a felsic plutonic assemblage
Quartz, K-feldspar and plagioclase in roughly equal proportions
solution: Basalt: fine-grained, mafic. Most abundant volcanic rock. Oceanic crust.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Corona texture, seen as reaction rims around minerals, results from which metamorphic process?
options: Incomplete reaction — mineral replacement textures. Olivine rimmed by orthopyroxene + spinel (granulite)
Complete equilibrium melting of the protolith leaving no residual minerals and producing a single homogeneous melt
Eutectic crystallization of the melt into discrete cumulate layers without any post-cumulus reaction
Mechanical mixing of different layers during sedimentary transport forming graded depositional units
solution: Corona: cooling (Opx + Sp around Ol). Kelyphite (Cpx + Sp around Grt). Reaction progress.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which option correctly describes the surface cut by wave erosion at the base of a sea cliff?
options: Steep vertical face of rock that retreats landward under wave attack
Feature formed by deposition of sediment rather than by erosion
Flat, gently sloping surface cut by wave erosion at cliff base
Elevated rock surface that lies permanently above the level of the sea
solution: Platform: erosional. Marine terrace: uplifted platform. Abrasion by sand and pebbles.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Normal mid-ocean ridge basalt (N-MORB) is derived from a depleted mantle source, as shown by what light REE pattern and (La/Sm)_N value?
options: Plume-derived mantle source with high ³He/⁴He and a strong positive Nb anomaly on primitive-mantle normalized diagrams
Enriched mantle source with elevated incompatible element concentrations
Depleted mantle source (light REE depleted). (La/Sm)_N < 1. ~6-8% partial melting of spinel lherzolite
Ocean island basalt source enriched by recycled oceanic crust and sediments
solution: N-MORB: La/Sm < 1. Depleted in incompatible elements. E-MORB: slightly enriched.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In the water table fluctuation method, groundwater recharge is estimated using:
options: Uses the drawdown of a pumping well to estimate specific storage
Applies the Theis equation to recovery data for aquifer parameters
Uses the steady state flow formula of Thiem for two wells
ΔS = S_y·ΔH. Recharge = S_y·dH/dt + discharge
solution: WTF: water table rise from precipitation. S_y from specific yield tests.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Crystal symmetry elements: rotation axes, mirror planes, inversion centers:
options: 14 groups. Symmetry combinations define the fourteen Bravais lattice types
Combination defines point group (32 crystallographic point groups)
7 groups. Each symmetry combination corresponds to one of the seven crystal systems
230 groups. The combinations yield every possible space group for minerals
solution: Point group: symmetry operations. Space group: point group + translations = 230 groups.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A dipping coal seam outcrops over a horizontal width of 80 m on flat ground and dips at 20°. Its true thickness is about:
solution: True thickness = horizontal width × sin(dip) = 80×sin20° ≈ 27.36 m.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: From the surface inward, the major layers of the Earth are:
options: Mantle, crust, core
Crust, mantle, core
Core, crust, mantle
Crust, core, mantle
solution: The Earth is layered into a thin crust, a thick mantle, and a metallic core.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Plagioclase feldspar typically shows which common type of twinning?
options: Commonly polysynthetic (albite twinning)
Occurs only in very slowly cooled plutonic rocks
Simple Carlsbad twinning on a single crystal scale
Twinning restricted to adjacent grains at grain contacts
solution: Plagioclase: polysynthetic twinning. Causes striations.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Radiocarbon (C-14) dating is applicable to organic material up to what maximum age, and what does it require?
options: ¹⁴C (T½ = 5730 yr). For organic material <50 ka. Atmospheric production, calibration curve
U-Pb method applied to zircon crystals extracted from the same strata body being studied, for ancient rocks
Rb-Sr method applied to whole-rock samples of the basement crystalline rocks below
K-Ar method applied to potassium minerals of the volcanic ash beds that are present
solution: C-14: radiocarbon. β⁻ decay. Libby (1949). Calibration: tree rings, corals, speleothems.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Geotechnical investigation borehole spacing depends on:
options: Site complexity and structure size
Only the overall height of the proposed structure
Only the financial budget allocated for the work
No fixed rule exists, spacing is purely arbitrary
solution: Borehole spacing: simple terrain large structures ~30-50m. Complex terrain small structures ~5-15m. BS 5930 guidance.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Seismic P-wave velocity in rocks generally increases with which rock properties?
options: Increasing rock density and elastic modulus
Increasing porosity filled with low density fluids
Decreasing temperature and increasing pore pressure
Decreasing density while shear modulus constant
solution: P-wave: Vp = sqrt((K+4/3G)/ρ). Higher density and modulus = higher velocity. Porosity decreases velocity.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The dip direction of cross-bedding in a sandstone bed indicates which direction?
options: Paleocurrent direction
Paleo-water depth at time of deposition
Provenance of the detrital sediment
Relative age of the sedimentary unit
solution: Cross-bedding: foresets dip in flow direction. Used for paleocurrent analysis. Restores paleogeography.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Diagenetic environment — meteoric phreatic:
options: Zone above the water table in the vadose zone, where only gravitational and meniscus cement forms between grains
Freshwater-saturated zone below water table. Equant/relict calcite cement. Dissolution common
Marine zone dominated by aragonite needle cement and micrite envelopes on all grains
Deep burial zone with pressure dissolution, stylolites and late ferroan calcite cement
solution: Meteoric phreatic: stable isotopes (δ¹⁸O depleted). Vadose: meniscus, gravitational cement.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Lineation in metamorphic rocks indicates:
options: Direction of maximum stretching
Orientation of original sedimentary bedding
Trace of the axial plane of a fold
Dip direction of the dominant fault plane
solution: Stretching lineation: alignment of elongate minerals. Indicates transport/stretching direction. Key kinematic indicator.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is a discordant tabular igneous intrusion that cross-cuts bedding?
options: Discordant tabular intrusion (cross-cuts bedding)
Concordant sheet intrusion emplaced parallel to the bedding planes
Horizontal intrusion that lies parallel to stratification of the host rock
Concordant intrusion that domes the strata above its flat floor
solution: Dyke: vertical or steeply dipping. Radiating or linear swarms.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Ultrahigh Temperature (UHT) metamorphism:
options: >900°C at 7-13 kbar. Sapphirine, orthopyroxene + sillimanite, osumilite. Lower crust
Eclogite facies metamorphism at pressures above 2.7 GPa during deep continental subduction
Blueschist facies conditions typical of cold subduction-zone environments at shallow mantle depths
Greenschist facies burial along a normal continental geothermal gradient at moderate crustal depths
solution: UHT: peak T >900°C. Mg-Al granulites. Eastern Ghats, Napier Complex (Antarctica).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which classification approach first segments an image, then classifies segments using shape and texture instead of pixels?
options: Segment image → classify segments (not pixels). Shape, texture, context. eCognition
Classify each pixel independently, using the spectral values only and ignoring all spatial context
Apply band-ratio indices to the whole image, without performing any segmentation step at all
Use per-pixel classifiers only, while ignoring the shape, texture and spatial context
solution: OBIA: multiresolution segmentation. Scale parameter. Feature space. Better than pixel for high-res.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A sequence boundary (SB) is a subaerial unconformity with its correlative conformity; a type 1 boundary differs from type 2 in that:
options: Condensed section with glauconite and pelagic sediment formed during the maximum flooding of the continental shelf
Subaerial unconformity + correlative conformity. Type 1 (Shelf exposed) vs Type 2 (shelf not exposed)
Maximum flooding surface marking the deepest water conditions
Transgressive surface recording the initial landward shift of the shoreline
solution: SB: base-level fall. Vail et al. (1977). Exxon sequence stratigraphy. Lowstand fan.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The gem mineral topaz crystallizes in which one of the following crystal systems?
options: Monoclinic system
Hexagonal system
Tetragonal system
Orthorhombic
solution: Topaz (Al2SiO4(F,OH)2) — orthorhombic. Hardness 8.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Gneiss, a high-grade metamorphic rock, is characteristically identified by which feature?
options: Vesicular holes formed by the escape of volcanic gases during eruption
Banding (segregation of light and dark minerals)
Abundant marine fossils preserved in a carbonate matrix
A glassy texture produced by the extremely rapid quenching of magma
solution: Gneiss is a high-grade foliated rock showing compositional banding (gneissic foliation).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal seam covers 1 km², is 3 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
options: 3 Mt
7.8 Mt
3.9 Mt
2 Mt
solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 1×10⁶ m²×3 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 3.9 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Accretionary wedge: deformed sediments scraped off subducting plate:
options: Oceanic crust and upper mantle rocks emplaced onto land by obduction
Thrust faults, mélanges, sedimentary rocks
High-grade metamorphic rocks brought up to the surface from great depth
Volcanic lava flows erupted along the convergent plate boundary
solution: Accretion: prism of deformed sediment. Offscraping, underplating. Mélanges: blocks in matrix.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which textural features are diagnostic of debrites (debris flow deposits) in the rock record?
options: Matrix-supported, poorly sorted clasts showing normal grading throughout
Clast-supported, well-sorted, rounded clasts with abundant imbrication
Matrix-supported, poorly sorted, angular clasts, no grading
Well-sorted, laminated sand with symmetrical wave ripple cross-lamination
solution: Debris flow: cohesive matrix support. High viscosity. Liquefied flow: fluid support.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How is the extinction angle of a mineral defined under crossed polars in thin section?
options: Not applicable to minerals that are studied in thin section preparations
Always 45° for every mineral regardless of orientation
Angle between cleavage and vibration direction under crossed polars
Always 90° in uniaxial minerals viewed along the optic axis
solution: Straight extinction: 0°. Oblique: 0-45°. Symmetrical: angle to both cleavages.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Metamorphic rocks are formed by the action of which agents on pre-existing rocks?
options: Evaporation and precipitation of dissolved salts from sea water
Rapid cooling of molten lava at the Earth's surface
Heat and/or pressure on pre-existing rocks
Cementation and compaction of transported detrital grains
solution: Metamorphism alters mineralogy and texture in the solid state under heat/pressure.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Calcareous nannofossils (coccoliths), typically under 30 µm and ranging from Cretaceous to Recent, are used for what?
options: Radiolaria. Siliceous nannoplankton (>30 µm) whose opaline tests are used chiefly in paleoceanographic reconstruction
Calcareous nannoplankton (<30 µm). Cretaceous-Recent. Biostratigraphy + paleoclimate. Emiliania huxleyi
Diatoms. Siliceous nannoplankton (<30 µm). Used chiefly for lacustrine and polar marine zonation
Foraminifera. Calcareous macrofossils (>2 mm). Zonation rests on benthic chamber morphology
solution: Nannofossils: produced by haptophyte algae. Chalk. High-resolution zonation for Cretaceous-Tertiary.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which factors primarily control the changes that occur during metamorphism of a rock?
options: Temperature and pressure acting alone on the protolith
Only the length of time the rock spends at depth
Chemical composition of the protolith and weathering intensity
Temperature, pressure, fluids (H2O, CO2), time
solution: T drives reactions. P controls mineral density. Fluids catalyze reactions.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How are tsunamis most commonly generated, and at what magnitude do thrust-fault earthquakes trigger them?
options: Ocean wave from underwater earthquake (M>7, thrust fault). Velocity ~√(gh)
Giant tidal wave caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun only
Slow surface current driven by wind and the Earth's rotation alone
Local storm surge generated by cyclonic winds blowing over the open sea
solution: Tsunami: long wavelength (>100 km). Wave height increases in shallow water. Run-up.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer (K = 10 m/day) of cross-section 100 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.01. The groundwater discharge is about:
options: 5 m³/day
10 m³/day
20 m³/day
1000 m³/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Unit cell: smallest repeating unit. For cubic: a=b=c, α=β=γ=90°. Volume:
options: V = abc, where a, b and c are the three cell edges
V = a³ (cubic)
V = a²c, valid for cubic and hexagonal lattices alike
V = a², giving the cell volume in square length units
solution: Cubic: V=a³. Tetragonal: V=a²c. Orthorhombic: V=abc. Hexagonal: V=a²c·sin(60°).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The compound eyes of trilobites are unique among arthropods because they are made of what mineral?
options: Aragonite prisms arranged in a simple lens array
Calcite crystals (unique among arthropods)
Silica spicules that form a single large biconvex lens
Chitinous lenses lacking any mineral reinforcement
solution: Trilobite eyes: calcite lenses. Holochroal (many lenses) or schizochroal (fewer, larger lenses).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Cosmogenic nuclide exposure dating (¹⁰Be, ²⁶Al):
options: No relationship between the nuclide concentration and the duration of exposure at the surface is known to exist at all
Concentration varies randomly with time and altitude of the surface exposure
Lower concentration always means longer exposure to the surface at all sites
Nucleides produced by cosmic rays in surface rocks. Higher concentration = longer exposure
solution: ¹⁰Be in quartz. Exposure age = N/(P×(1-e^{-λt})). For surfaces >100ka.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In geostatistics, kriging interpolation is best described as which type of estimator?
options: Simple arithmetic averaging of all sample grades falling within the block being estimated for the resource
Linear regression of grade against a single regional structural trend surface
Best linear unbiased estimator (BLUE). Uses variogram. Weighted average of neighbors
Random selection of the nearest sample value to represent the entire block grade
solution: Kriging: minimize estimation variance. Weights from variogram. Ordinary: unknown mean. Simple: known mean.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An ore body of 1 Mt has an average metal grade of 3%. The contained metal is about:
options: 3 kt
15 kt
30 kt
60 kt
solution: Metal = tonnage × grade = 1 Mt × 3% = 30 thousand tonnes (kt).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Epithermal gold deposits are subdivided into which two classes based on their alteration and mineralogy?
options: Banded iron formation precipitated from stratified Precambrian seawater
Deep plutonic lode deposits formed at several kilometres depth in batholiths
Porphyry copper stockwork vein systems with potassic alteration and disseminated sulfide mineralization
Low sulfidation (quartz-adularia) vs high sulfidation (enargite). Hot springs. Au-Ag
solution: Epithermal: <300°C, <1.5 km. Hishikari (Japan), Yanacocha (Peru). Bonanza grades.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Coal bed methane is stored in coal primarily by which mechanism, and how is it recovered?
options: Free gas occupying the interconnected pore porosity of conventional sandstone reservoir rocks trapped beneath structural and stratigraphic closures
Tight gas stored in low-permeability shale and carbonate source rocks
Methane adsorbed in coal matrix. Sweet spots: high rank, good permeability. Recovery: dewatering → desorption
Oil shale yielding liquid hydrocarbons through retorting of kerogen-rich strata
solution: CBM: shallow (300-1500m). Proppantless fracturing. Coal rank: high-volatile bituminous best.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Volcanogenic massive sulfide deposits, formed by submarine volcanic exhalative activity, are enriched in which metals?
options: Lateritic enrichment of nickel and cobalt by intense tropical chemical weathering
Sedimentary exhalation of Zn-Pb-Ag brines into reducing anoxic rift basin waters on the ancient seafloor
Mechanical concentration of heavy resistant minerals by fluvial and beach processes
Cu-Zn-Pb ± Au-Ag. Submarine volcanic exhalative. Kuroko (Japan), Noranda, Kidd Creek
solution: VMS: stratiform, lens-shaped. Stringer zone (feeder) + massive ore. Besshi, Cyprus, Kuroko types.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A rock retains 25% of its original parent isotope (half-life 1.3 Gyr). Its radiometric age is about:
options: 0.65 Gyr
2.6 Gyr
1.3 Gyr
3.9 Gyr
solution: 25% remaining ⇒ 2 half-lives ⇒ age = 2×1.3 = 2.6 Gyr.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: On the block diagram shown, the inclined bedding plane dips at 30°. The dip direction is, by definition:
options: Parallel to the strike, measured along the line of the bedding plane outcrop at the surface
Perpendicular to the strike, in the direction of steepest descent
Vertical regardless of the strike, so dip direction always points straight downward
Horizontal along the strike in whatever direction the bedding plane is gently inclined
solution: Dip (here 30°) is measured perpendicular to strike, down the line of steepest slope of the plane.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+25+15) = 56%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Darcy's law for groundwater flow states that the discharge Q is equal to:
options: Q = K·i where K is the permeability and i is the hydraulic gradient alone
Q = i·A with i being the hydraulic gradient and A the cross sectional area of flow
Q = K·i·A. K = hydraulic conductivity, i = hydraulic gradient, A = area
Q = K·A where K is the hydraulic conductivity and A the area of flow
solution: Darcy: laminar flow. Valid for Re < 10. K = k·ρ·g/μ (intrinsic permeability).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The most abundant group of rock-forming minerals in the Earth's crust is the:
options: Carbonates
Silicates
Sulphides
Oxides
solution: Silicate minerals (feldspar, quartz, mica, etc.) dominate the crust.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes the hypsometric curve and what its shape indicates about basin erosion stage?
options: Curve that plots the width of a river valley against its distance downstream measured from the headwater source region of the river
Curve that plots the total length of a river channel against its elevation above mean sea level measured at every kilometre along the channel course
Erosion stage (youth, mature, old). Area-altitude relationship. Young = convex (upper), old = concave (lower)
Curve that plots the volume of water discharge against the time of year at a gauging station along the river course
solution: Hypsometry: integral = area under curve. High integral > 0.6 (youthful).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which remote sensing classification method uses training samples of known classes to classify all remaining pixels in an image?
options: Training samples (known classes) → classify rest of image. Maximum likelihood
Clustering of the pixels into groups, without using any analyst-defined training data at all
Automatic labelling of the pixels, using a set of predefined spectral thresholds values
A purely manual photo-interpretation of the image, with no training samples being used
solution: Supervised: user-defined training areas. Unsupervised: algorithm clusters pixels. Hybrid approach common.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How does earthquake magnitude (energy) differ from intensity (observed damage) in reporting an event?
options: Magnitude measures damage while intensity measures the energy released
Magnitude (Richter, Mw) — energy. Intensity (MMI) — damage
Both magnitude and intensity are identical scales of the same quantity
Intensity is measured only by instruments; magnitude is judged visually
solution: Moment magnitude (Mw): most accurate. MMI: I (not felt) to XII (total destruction).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Bowen's reaction series: discontinuous branch (mafic minerals):
options: Olivine -> Pyroxene -> Amphibole -> Biotite (increasing silica content)
Fixed order of crystallisation that does not depend on temperature
Crystallisation of a single mineral phase throughout the cooling interval
Reverse order in which biotite crystallises before olivine at high temperature
solution: Discontinuous: olivine (early, high T) to biotite (late, lower T). Continuous: Ca-plagioclase to Na-plagioclase.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What are the major subdivisions of the Siwalik Group and their representative formations?
options: Two divisions, an older marine shelf unit and a younger deltaic unit of the foredeep basin margin
Lower (Kamliyal), Middle (Nagri, Dhok Pathan), Upper (Tatrot, Pinjor, Boulder Conglomerate)
Five divisions based entirely on the changing grain size of the conglomerates present
Four divisions of equal thickness defined on the basis of cyclic bedding repetition
solution: Siwalik: molasse (Himalayan erosion). Hominoid fossils (Ramapithecus). Thickness >5000m.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In carbonate diagenesis, what does neomorphism refer to, and what is its typical outcome?
options: Replacement of limestone by microcrystalline quartz derived from biogenic silica during early burial diagenesis
Replacement of aragonite or calcite by calcite of different crystal size (aggrading neomorphism)
Complete dissolution of carbonate minerals followed by precipitation of new blocky calcite in all pores
Replacement of calcite by dolomite in magnesium-rich brines during shallow burial diagenesis
solution: Neomorphism: wet transformation. Microspar → pseudospar. Aragonite → calcite inversion.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Contact (thermal) metamorphism is produced mainly by what, and where does it occur relative to an intrusion?
options: Regional pressure acting over an entire orogenic belt
Heat from intrusion. Aureole around pluton
Shock wave from a large meteorite impact event
Hot seawater circulation along mid-ocean ridges
solution: Contact: high T, low P. Hornfels. Spotted slates near intrusion.
